title: Microwave ovens don’t work by ‘resonating’ water molecules
body: A popular explanation says microwave ovens are tuned to a special resonance of water. They aren’t: most home ovens run at about 2.45 GHz, a radio band set aside for such uses, and water has no sharp resonance there. Instead, the rapidly flipping electric field keeps twisting polar molecules like water, which have a positive and a negative end, and their jostling becomes heat. This dielectric heating works across a wide range of frequencies.

slides.question: At what frequency, in megahertz, do most home microwave ovens run?
slides.explanation: About 2,450 MHz (2.45 GHz), a radio band set aside worldwide for such uses; 915 MHz is set aside only in some countries. Water has no sharp resonance there.

slides.question: Why do most home microwave ovens run at about 2.45 GHz?
options: A radio band is reserved for such uses
It matches the size of a plate
slides.explanation: That frequency sits in a radio band set aside for such uses. Water has no sharp resonance there, and dielectric heating works across a wide range of frequencies.

slides.heading: Which one doesn’t absorb microwaves?
slides.explanation: Water, sugars and fats are polar molecules that soak up microwave energy and heat. Metal reflects microwaves, which is why a metal pot keeps them from the food.
